analysis: Reviewed the supplied units: two head_text chunks of docs/developer/test.md (lines 1844-2538), the metadata-only unit for scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py, and its patch. The test.md changes visible in file_changes are documentation only (CI shard lane routing note at ~99-101 and a route-test description at ~1371-1374). The supplied head text is test-procedure prose covering batch, prefix-cache, tenant-partition and SSD-record checks. It adds no code, endpoints, key handling or policy changes. The prose describes existing tests, notes that they establish no hardware or security qualification, and states that the tenant-partition and prefix-record checks are synthetic. It does not weaken any retained control. T-041 (the cache TTL, HMAC lookup and salt-scoping invariants) is not altered. The scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py patch is a CI routing test harness. It introduces a SHARDED set so that each test-provider matrix shard reads its own lane (test-provider-N). It also adds helpers (matrix_shards, job_lanes, requested_lanes) and updates the assertions. This is test-only code that parses workflow YAML text with regexes and runs the router script against temporary files. It handles no secrets and no untrusted runtime input beyond repo files. The router tests still pin route permissions as {}, no secrets, literal runners for release workflows, and fallback labels. The workflow YAML (ci.yml, darkbloom-route.yml) is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify that the workflow actually requests the per-shard lanes. That is a CI availability and consistency matter rather than a provider or coordinator trust boundary, and the test would fail if it were mismatched. The patch excerpt is truncated, so unseen portions of the script were not examined. I identified no security regression and no threat-model update is needed.
